customer_question: What does the 'Q30' prefix on a QDID mean? Is it less official than an older-format QDID number?
question_variants: Are Q30-prefix QDIDs the same as old QDIDs legally?
When does Combine unmodified Designs produce a Design Number?
actual_issue: The Q30 prefix is the QDID format introduced by QPRDv3.0 (post-July 2024). It has exactly the same legal standing as pre-QPRDv3.0 numeric QDIDs. Additionally: when 'Combine unmodified Designs' is used, a Design Number (with Q30 prefix) is auto-assigned only if 2 or more QDIDs are combined. If only 1 QDID is referenced, no Design Number is assigned — the entry shows 'Details' instead.
plain_english_explanation: The Q30 prefix just means the QDID was issued under the QPRDv3.0 system. Customers who see it for the first time sometimes worry it is a lesser or temporary ID — it is not. It is the current standard format and has the same legal weight as any older numeric QDID. Separately, when combining existing QDIDs via 'Combine unmodified Designs,' the system will auto-assign a Q30-format Design Number only if there are 2 or more QDIDs in the combination.
consultant_answer: Q30 prefix = QPRDv3.0 format QDID. Same legal force as older QDIDs. 'Combine unmodified Designs' auto-assigns a Q30 Design Number only when ≥2 QDIDs are combined; 1 QDID → no DN (shows 'Details').
decision_logic:
1. Q30 prefix: new format since QPRDv3.0 — legally equivalent to old QDIDs.
2. Combine unmodified Designs: ≥2 QDIDs → Q30 DN auto-assigned; 1 QDID → no DN (entry shows 'Details').
final_recommendation: Reassure customers that Q30 QDIDs are fully valid. When using Combine unmodified Designs, plan to have ≥2 QDIDs if a Design Number is needed for product listing or product identification purposes.
risk_if_done_wrong: If a customer needs a Design Number (e.g., to list their product in the SIG member directory) and only has 1 QDID to combine, Combine unmodified Designs will not produce one — they need a different approach.
